description: The intersection loop at lines 1290-1327 is O(current × new) per cert. With k CA certs each adding m subtrees, the intersection is O(m²) per cert × k certs = O(k × m²). For typical chains (k≤5, m≤10) this is fine. However nc_excluded uses extend() (union, append-only): excluded list grows monotonically with no deduplication. check_name_constraints calls nc_excluded.as_slice() and iterates it for every name in every cert. With a 100-cert chain each adding 10 excluded entries, nc_excluded has 1000 entries, and checking each cert's SAN list (say 5 names) requires 5000 comparisons. Not catastrophic but O(certs² × names). The deduplication miss in nc_excluded is the main concern — excluded entries from the same constraint repeated across multiple certs via extend cause redundant work. Expected impact: negligible for chains ≤20 certs and ≤20 SANs; may matter for long enterprise chains.
title: NC permitted subtree intersection is O(n²) per cert × O(n) certs = O(n³)
